answer: Each identity holds one distinct FCC low-power FM licence on a unique frequency near its lagoon transmitter site. Verifiers at random hours require a live broadcast of a fresh cipher nonce seeded by its key, matched to logged power and its spiral antenna pattern. Sharing a transmitter or missing two checks revokes the slot and burns a 5-coin bond. Spectrum is scarce: 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 licences, transmitters at $2,500 each ($2.5 million) plus $180 monthly power and rent each, no frequency reusable in one market. Trade-off: scarcity caps growth and rural applicants face long waits.
